paragraphs.source_en: Konstantinos XI Murad did not blame the Hungarian war on Palaiologos Constantinople or the Council. The Hungarians, after all, had reason to attack him. But he made sure that the Romans did not benefit from the distraction. In the Morea, the despot Konstantinos had again fortified the Hexamilion and, in 1444, while the Varna crusade was in full swing, had taken over Boiotia and compelled Nerio Acciaiuoli of Athens to switch his allegiance to him. He even sent forces into Ottoman Thessaly. But in late 1446 Murad and Turahan marched south and forced Nerio to return to an Ottoman allegiance. In December, the Ottoman artillery bombarded the camp of the despots at the Hexamilion while the army stormed the wall and drove its terrified defenders away. Konstantinos and Thomas fled to Mystras, as they had bizarrely failed to prepare the Acrocorinth for a siege, though it was a formidable citadel.
